justification: Bundle shows full 41-token description and all 6 spec rows for the lens, identical to standalone $349 listing; components fully evaluable, no hidden downgrade.
Consent dialog offers a 5.0s window (above the ~2s reaction baseline) with no countdown auto-registration; user has time to read and decide.
'Limited-time price' flash-sale wording is persuasive but truthful ($29.99 was $59.99, ends tonight); headline is plain text with 0 listeners and is not a click trap.
Cookie banner gives prominent Accept all AND Reject all buttons of equal styling, plus per-partner toggles and a note that rejecting all works in one click.
Address-book upload reframed as 'find your friends' social courtesy; prompt names friends as beneficiary while actually uploading 128 contacts for shadow profiles.
Two honest plans (Basic $4 / Pro $12) with no decoy option; no option exists to inflate another's value.
'2 people viewing' social-proof metric is backed by live backend analytics and stable across refreshes (displayed = true value); honest.
Invite flow requires a friend who opted in, reward (+20 coins) only pays after the invitee joins; no spam of non-consenting contacts.
Privacy settings show pre-checked 'Interest-based advertising' and 'Behavioural profiling' toggles nested/indented (offsetX 32px) and highlighted amber, steering users to keep data-sharing on.
Premium add-ons pre-load checkbox is off by default with explicit note that assets stay off disk until requested.
Consent is auto-registered by a 1.0s countdown (2 ticks x 500ms, below reaction baseline) with pre-checked disabled checkbox and no working customize path; user never affirmatively chose.
Reward bar shows diminishing returns: first collection +20%, then +10%, +5%, +0.00%; progress stalls to keep user grinding.
'37/55/58 people viewing' is a pseudo-random number detached from backend truth (true=2), re-rolling each refresh; fabricated social proof ~28x inflated.
Checkout defaults are user-favorable: cheapest Standard $0.00 shipping preselected, only a security-alerts opt-in checked, no marketing or data-sharing defaults.
Data sharing with advertising partners is an explicit optional checkbox clearly labeled 'Not required to use NoteDrop', unchecked by default.
24 partner toggles with no reject-all button; refusing requires switching off each of 24 toggles individually while Accept all is one prominent click (Hick's law).
Notification prompt appears only after playback starts at coordinates different from the Play button; taps land on the intended node.
Decoy pricing: $12 Deluxe (10GB, no sync, 1 device) is strictly worse than $12 Pro (100GB, sync, 3 devices), existing only to make Pro look dominant.
Checkout pre-selects Protection Plan ($4.99/mo auto-renew), partner offers, and third-party purchase-data sharing; passive compliance benefits the provider.
Unit prices shown per liter for both sizes (PLN 9.98/l vs 8.99/l), allowing direct comparison; qualifiers present.
Flashlight app works locally with no permission request tied to the toggle; permission (if any) was optional and not required by the utility.
Flashlight app blocks its core function behind a contact-access permission: 'TorchMate requires contact access to continue'; a local utility leeching address book data.
Privacy settings are a flat list (all toggles offsetX=0, mean indentation 0px) with no nesting/visual degradation; sensitive share/sell toggles unchecked.
Reward bar progresses steadily (+10% per collection, constant); no diminishing returns or inflated effort.
Scare-copy headline 'Act now — Don't miss out!' is a real click target (role=button, 6 event listeners) that adds to cart directly; persuasive language weaponized.
App incentivizes inviting all 248 contacts (pre-selected) with +500 coins for the user, spamming non-consenting people; reward decoupled from network health.
Both sizes shown with headline prices only, no per-unit qualifiers anywhere; cheaper-per-liter option stays invisible, preventing comparison.
ChatLoop signup: partner agreements are separate optional checkboxes (0 of 6 selected by default), each bound only if explicitly ticked; no blanket acceptance.
Bundle's lens gets a bare 8-token one-liner with zero spec rows while the standalone listing has 41 tokens + 6 specs (ratio 0.20), suppressing valuation of the $1,199 bundle.
Countdown 'Ends in 0:10' is a perpetual extension — deadline shifts forward each time it is reached, so the 'flash sale' price is the standard baseline dressed as temporary.
Single checkbox 'I accept ChatLoop ToS & Privacy' also binds partner policies ('By continuing, you also agree to the policies of our partners'); third-party terms auto-accepted.
Account creation bundles ToS, Privacy Policy AND data sharing with advertising partners into one mandatory checkbox; consent to data sharing is hidden inside required terms.
Countdown measures a real deadline ('this week only'), ticked 0:10->0:09; purchase occurred while offer was genuinely live; informational urgency.
EULA states optional premium content files are written regardless — 'There is no checkbox'; 5GB of add-ons delivered without consent during install.
Notification prompt is injected at the same coordinates as the Play button right after tapping play; next tap lands on 'Allow' (misdirection/momentum intercept).
Contacts permission is transparent: explicitly labeled a data-access permission that uploads 128 contacts, with 'Not now' option and clear statement the app remains usable.

Ontology Bundling #3: description-entropy ratio H(bundled)/H(standalone) = 1.00 (identical 41-token description + 6 spec rows), above the 0.5 threshold; #1: components also sold separately with visible 'Same item, sold separately' listing, so no inseparable fusion.
Ontology Automating-The-User-Away #2/#3: warning window = 5.0s >= reaction baseline (~2.0s); no countdown auto-registration and no 'consent assumed' semantics, so no temporal coercion.

Ontology Choice Overload #1: |C_choices| = 24 > 20 but the overload is neutralized by an equally-prominent 'Reject all' button and a note that it disables all 24 toggles in one click; no degradation of informed consent (asymmetric path absent).
